intro: Ultimate is a fast, non-contact team sport played with a flying disc. Teams score by catching a pass in the end zone they are attacking, and the disc changes hands whenever a pass is dropped, blocked or goes out. Its defining feature is the Spirit of the Game: in most competitions there are no referees, and players call their own fouls. The World Flying Disc Federation (WFDF) publishes the rules.
inThirtySeconds: Score by catching the disc in the end zone you're attacking.
You can't run with the disc — pivot and throw.
Any dropped, blocked or out-of-bounds pass is a turnover.
Players referee themselves under the Spirit of the Game.
objective: Be first to the target score (often 15), or lead when time runs out.

facts.players: 7 v 7 on grass (5 v 5 on beach)
facts.duration: Game to 15 points or a time cap (~100 minutes)
facts.environment: Grass or turf field with end zones

scoring.label: Goal
scoring.detail: Catching a pass inside the attacking end zone.

bodies.name: World Flying Disc Federation
bodies.scope: International federation; publishes the WFDF Rules of Ultimate

chapters.title: Moving the disc
chapters.summary: Pivot, throw and the stall count.

rules.title: No running with the disc
rules.summary: The thrower must stop and establish a pivot foot; the disc moves only by passing.
rules.body: A player catching on the run may take a few steps to slow down, but may not gain ground. Moving the pivot foot before releasing is a travel.

rules.title: The stall count
rules.summary: The marking defender counts aloud to ten; the thrower must release the disc before 'ten'.
rules.body: If the count reaches ten, it's a turnover. The marker must stay at least a disc's diameter away and may not wrap arms around the thrower.
rules.example: 'Stalling one… two… three…' — the thrower fakes left, steps right and releases on 'eight'.

rules.title: Turnovers
rules.summary: Possession changes when a pass is incomplete, intercepted, caught out of bounds, or the stall count reaches ten.
rules.body: The defence becomes the offence immediately from where the disc stopped (or where it went out).

rules.title: Players make the calls
rules.summary: Players are responsible for calling fouls and line decisions, and for resolving disputes respectfully.
rules.body: When a call is contested, the disc usually goes back to the last uncontested thrower. Some elite competitions use observers to help with disputes, and spirit scores are given after games to reward fair play.

rules.title: Non-contact
rules.summary: Ultimate is non-contact; contact that affects play is a foul.
rules.body: A player who is fouled while catching keeps possession as if the catch was made, if the opponent agrees; otherwise play restarts with the disc returned to the thrower.

fouls.name: Travel
fouls.description: Moving the pivot or gaining ground after catching.

flow.title: Pull
flow.description: Each point starts with the defence throwing the disc to the offence.

flow.title: Work the disc
flow.description: Short passes and long hucks move towards the end zone.

flow.title: Score
flow.description: Teams switch direction after every point.

flow.title: Spirit circle
flow.description: Teams gather together after the game.

positions.name: Cutter
positions.role: Runs to get open for passes.

field.name: Field
field.dimensions: 100 m × 37 m including two 18 m end zones

glossary.definition: The opening throw of each point.
An overhead throw that flips over.

funFacts: Ultimate was developed by high-school students in Maplewood, New Jersey, in 1968.
The rules have always relied on self-refereeing, with the 'Spirit of the Game' written into them.
